sentences.text: This dinosaur had a skull that was relatively wide and low.
The back surface of the supraoccipital bone, a part of the skull roof, leaned forward at roughly 45 degrees, unlike the nearly vertical orientation seen in older relatives.
Despite its size, this creature could walk on two legs or four legs while eating plants.
A team of eight scientists led by Run-Fu Wang officially named the animal in 2013.
The name Yunganglong combines the Chinese word for dragon with a reference to the famous Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site located about 50 kilometers away.
The specific name datongensis honors the city of Datong in northern Shanxi Province, where the main fossil was found.
We know this dinosaur only from a single disarticulated partial skeleton cataloged as SXMG V 00001, which is kept at the Shanxi Museum of Geology.
Workers collected the bones in 2011 for a project run by the Department of Land and Resources of Shanxi Province.
Fossils of armored ankylosaurs and horned ceratopsians were also uncovered at these same locations.
The genus contains only one known species, Yunganglong datongensis.
It belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
The animal is classified within the infraorder Iguanodontia.
Phylogenetic analysis places Yunganglong as more advanced than Probactrosaurus, within an unresolved group with other early hadrosauroids like Jintasaurus and Protohadros.
Fossils were found in the lower Zhumapu Formation in Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province, in northeastern China.
Yunganglong lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 100 to 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
